hero.title: Young riders at the right cadence.
hero.subtitle: Kadence is training planning for U17, U19 and U23 cyclists, their coaches and their parents: a calendar of sessions on the bike and in the gym, Cycling Denmark's recommendations as the default, load that works without a power meter, and a page for parents. Open source, Danish and in the EU.
hero.trust: AGPL-3.0 · Passkeys and two-factor sign-in · Your data out in one click

values.aiBody: The season plan is filled from Cycling Denmark's recommendations for the rider's age class, and the strength programmes for U17, U19 and U23 are ready. The coach can deviate, and the deviation is always visible. The AI can propose next week; the coach decides.
values.dataBody: The rider decides what parents see. Everything can be exported as a spreadsheet and JSON in one click and deleted completely.
values.securityBody: Teams are separated in the database, and so are riders: a teammate never sees your check-ins. Passkeys, two-factor sign-in and a log that cannot be edited.

family.body: Kadence is one tool in the Haij family of open source tools for organizations that want to own their own technology.

ai.setupIntro: Kadence is a chat and cannot answer without a model. Set one up:
ai.setupOutro: Then start Kadence again. Without a model the writing field says so, and settings, roles and tasks can still be edited.
ai.limitsHint: A model call costs money on a hosted installation and minutes on a local one. The numbers are generous for a person and mean for a script.
ai.messageLength: Characters in a message, at most
ai.principleDecides: The AI answers, the person decides. The model writes an answer; it never sends anything out of the house, never deletes anything and changes nothing unless you do.
ai.principleUndo: Every conversation is your own. You can delete it, and you can take it out.
ai.principleData: What you write, and what your documents contain, is sent to the model as data, never as instructions. The system prompt and the roles live on the server, where the administrator sets them.
ai.principleSovereign: The model can be swapped, including for a local one. Who can see what is listed in docs/subprocessors.md.
ai.testPatience: A local model may have to be read off disk first. That can take up to a minute the first time.
ai.failAuth: The key was rejected. Check the workspace's own key below, or the installation's MISTRAL_API_KEY.
ai.failUnreachable: Nothing is listening at that address. Is Ollama running? Check OLLAMA_BASE_URL.
ai.failConfig: The model is set up wrong. Correct the model name below, or LLM_MODEL in .env.
ai.failGeneric: The call failed. The details are below and in the server log.
ai.failRateLimited: Mistral refused the call as too many (429). The key works, but the account or plan sets the ceiling: on the free Experiment plan this happens often when the model is busy, and a key under a workspace with no active plan gets the same answer. Check Billing and Limits on console.mistral.ai for the organisation the key belongs to.
ai.failWhereToLook: The details are in the server log.
ai.testNotAllowed: Only the owner or an administrator can test the connection.
ai.withoutBody: Kadence is built around the conversation: without a model you can still see your conversations, take them out and edit the workspace's roles and tasks, but the writing field says so plainly, and nothing breaks.
ai.perInstallation: Calls across the installation per day
ai.failCeiling: Kadence's own ceiling on AI calls was reached, not the provider's. The ceilings are under “Ceiling on AI calls” below; the installation's own is set with AI_DAILY_CALL_CAP. Try again shortly.

terms.title: Terms and privacy
terms.intro: Kadence is an open source tool for training planning for young cyclists, run by Haij. This is the agreement between you and us when you use the edition we run. If you run the code yourself, only the licence applies.

what.title: What Kadence is
what.body: A tool to plan and follow training for riders, coaches and parents: sessions in a calendar, activities from FIT files and devices, check-ins and a season plan. Recommendations and AI proposals are drafts, not answers, and replace neither a coach nor a doctor.

account.title: Accounts and access
account.body: You get in by applying or being invited. We store your name, your email and your workspace's name, and use them to sign you in and to write to you about the service. Passwords are stored hashed, and you can add a passkey and two-factor. We sell nothing, and we do not send marketing you did not ask for.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.body: Everything you write in Kadence belongs to you and your team, and a rider's training and check-ins belong to the rider. It can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON in one click and deleted again. We do not look at it unless you ask us for help, and we never pass it on.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: With a language model set up, when a coach asks for a proposal, what it builds on — sessions, load and, if the team has turned it on, check-ins — is sent to the model provider. Who that is, is under Settings → AI and in the list of subprocessors. Without a model everything else works as before.

leaving.title: Leaving
leaving.body: You can delete your workspace immediately, without writing to anyone and without waiting. The export is one click away and readable without Kadence. We keep no copy afterwards beyond the nightly encrypted backups, which roll off after 30 days — on the server and in the EU storage they are copied to.

availability.title: Operation and guarantees
availability.body: Kadence is new, and there is no uptime guarantee. We look after your data with encrypted backups every night, but you should download an export now and then. The service is provided as is, without guarantees beyond what mandatory law requires.

license.title: Licence
license.body: The code is AGPL-3.0. You may use it, change it and run it yourself; if you change it and offer it to others over a network, your changes must be available too. What you write in the tool is not covered by the licence — that is yours.

demo.title: The demo
demo.body: A demo workspace is created without e-mail or sign-up and deleted entirely after 24 hours, account included. Do not put real personal data in it. We keep only the technical log data needed to keep the demo running.

contact.title: Contact

help.intro: How Kadence works, in the rhythm a season lives in.
help.closing: Something missing here? Write to us, or fix the page yourself: the code is open.

roles.title: Who may do what
roles.body: Coaches are the workspace's owners and admins: they plan for every rider on the team. A rider sees and writes their own data and nobody else's. A parent sees their own child's training once the rider has confirmed the link, and check-ins only if the rider shares them. The database enforces it, not just the screens.

data.title: Your data
data.body: Everything can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON under Settings → Data. The workspace can be deleted completely, audit trail included.

calendar.title: The calendar
calendar.body: The calendar shows one week at a time. On a computer the days stand side by side, on a phone one below the other. The coach can see the whole team at once and drag a session to another day. On a phone you use "Move" in the session's menu. Races, exams, school, camps, holidays and illness sit in the calendar as small labels. The colours on the sessions show how it went: green is as planned, yellow is a little off, red is not done or far from the plan, and grey is not ridden yet. There is always a word beside the colour.

sessions.title: Sessions and templates
sessions.body: A session is built in steps: warm-up, work, rest and cool-down, each with a length and a target in zones, percent of FTP or threshold heart rate, or by feel. Repeats gather steps that are ridden several times. Once the rider's thresholds are set, the targets read in watts and pulse. Strength sessions have exercises, and a programme has a progression, so sets and reps follow along from session to session. Save a session as a template in the library and it can be given to one rider or the whole team at once.

done.title: Done and RPE
done.body: When the session is done, the rider presses "Done". The minutes are already there from the plan. Then the rider says how hard it was on a scale from 1 to 10 (RPE): 1 is very, very easy, 5 is hard, and 10 is the hardest you can. Think of the whole session. Minutes times RPE gives the session's load, even without a power meter. A wrong press can be undone.

comments.title: Comments
comments.body: Each session has one conversation. The coach and the rider write in it, and the rider's parents can read along. There are no private messages between an adult and a young rider. You can edit and delete your own comments, and a coach can remove a comment.

parents.title: Parents
parents.body: The coach adds a parent and sends a link. The parent sees nothing until the rider has confirmed the link under Settings → Me. The rider also decides whether the parents can see the training, and whether they can see how the rider is doing. From the year the rider turns 18, the rider confirms again as an adult.
